definitions.explanation: An X-ray image or X-ray examination. Named after Wilhelm Röntgen, the discoverer of X-rays. Used in everyday Japanese to refer to both the procedure and the resulting image.

examples.japanese: レントゲンで{骨折|こっせつ}が{見|み}つかった。
examples.english: A fracture was found on the X-ray.

examples.japanese: {健康|けんこう}{診断|しんだん}で{胸|むね}のレントゲンを{撮|と}ってもらった。
examples.english: I had a chest X-ray taken during my health checkup.

notes:
レントゲン is the standard everyday word for X-ray in Japanese, named after Wilhelm Röntgen. The more technical term is エックス{線|せん} (X-ray).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- レントゲンを{撮|と}る: to take an X-ray
- レントゲン{写真|しゃしん}: X-ray photograph
- レントゲン{検査|けんさ}: X-ray examination
- {胸|むね}のレントゲン: chest X-ray

NOTE:
In everyday conversation, レントゲン is far more common than エックス{線|せん}. It is used by both patients and medical staff in casual settings, while エックス{線|せん} appears in formal medical documentation.
